name: North Cascades National Park
blurb: Glaciers, old-growth forest and the goats, lynx and cougars of the high Cascades.

tip.title: Lose the whitebark pine
tip.text: Whitebark pine seeds feed nutcrackers, squirrels and bears. Set Whitebark pine to -100% and watch the nutcracker, the squirrel and the bear that depend on its seeds.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Along with western red cedar and Douglas fir, it dominates the low, wet valleys of the park, where old-growth forest covers a large area.
A soft-leaved shrub of forest openings. Its leaves and berries are eaten by deer, hares, bears and bumble bees.
A tall wildflower that spreads quickly across burned or cleared ground and is browsed by mule deer.
A high-elevation pine whose large seeds feed nutcrackers, squirrels and bears. Blister rust and pine beetles have killed many of the park trees.
Cuts and stores cones in middens and eats conifer seeds. Bears raid whitebark pine middens for seeds.
A browser that eats wildflowers, shrubs and conifer foliage, and is a main prey of cougars. The park lists Columbia black-tailed deer, a mule deer form, as a common sight.
Browses shrubs and young plants through the year. It is the staple prey of the Canada lynx.
Grazes alpine and subalpine slopes on grasses, herbs, shrubs and twigs. Cougars are probably its main predator, with eagles taking kids.
A big ground squirrel of alpine meadows that eats grasses and flowering plants, then hibernates through the long snowy winter.
Gathers meadow plants into hay piles in rock slides. Sensitive to heat, so warming mountain slopes are a concern.
The main disperser of whitebark pine. It buries thousands of seeds each year, and the ones it forgets can grow into new trees.
A snow-adapted cat reported in the park that specializes on snowshoe hares.
A bird of prey listed among the park raptors. It hunts marmots and hares in open country and can take goat kids.
A clever omnivore that scavenges carcasses such as deer and goats and also eats seeds and small animals.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: A large cat whose main prey is deer and other hoofed animals. Likely the top predator of mountain goats.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats berries, whitebark pine seeds raided from squirrel middens, and sometimes deer, goats and hares.
The park has about 312 glaciers. Melt feeds cold streams in late summer, but the ice is shrinking.
Large natural fires are rare and come every few decades to centuries, and lightning fires are often allowed to burn.
Holds the nutrients and moisture that the forests and meadows draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen logs, needles, carcasses and dung and return nutrients to the soil.
